extracted.intended_audience: UW–Madison faculty, researchers, and staff preparing grant proposals (especially NIH/USDA/NSF applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing competitive university research grant proposals with emphasis on NIH-style applications and USDA/NSF funder expectations; includes UW-specific resources, pre-submission checks, and funder-tailored emphasis. Useful for faculty and research staff preparing proposals at UW–Madison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard four-paragraph structure; hypothesis-driven aims; aim independence emphasized; conceptual figure encouraged; iterate 10+ times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conventional four-paragraph Specific Aims structure, make aims hypothesis-driven and independent from one another, include a conceptual figure to orient reviewers, and iterate the page many times (recommendation: 10+ iterations) to sharpen clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame significance for non-specialist reviewers and 'land' the importance quickly (significance landed in 30 seconds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect the problem to high-impact recent literature, tie to funder/NIH institute mission when applicable, and make the importance immediately apparent to reviewers outside the subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight novelty, framed as a feasible or novel application rather than speculative novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what is new about the approach/concept and how it advances the field; present innovation in a way that is credible and connected to the project's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (aim-level detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each aim should have subsections detailing experimental plans, with statistical analysis plan, power calculation, and sample size justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize Approach by aim, include explicit statistical methods, justify sample sizes with power calculations, describe alternatives, and show how results will be interpreted relative to hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state rigor practices and reproducibility measures (authentication of resources, consideration of sex as a biological variable, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements on authentication of reagents/resources, blinding/randomization where appropriate, transparent reporting, and how the study design addresses reproducibility concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary quantitative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative preliminary data that supports feasibility of the proposed aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data demonstrating feasibility and informing power/sample size; emphasize quantitative results rather than only descriptive observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator and environment fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity appropriate to career stage; independence narrative for Early-Stage Investigators (ESI); cite UW-specific resources and institutional strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the investigator section to show expertise and independence (especially for ESI), describe mentoring/training as needed, and enumerate institutional resources that support success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters should be specific, describing concrete commitments and relevance rather than generic endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain letters that spell out resource access, collaborations, and explicit roles; avoid boilerplate letters that do not add evaluative weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of UW cores and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage and cite relevant UW cores and facilities (e.g., UW Biotechnology Center, WID, Carbone Cancer Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention specific core facilities and how they will be used to strengthen feasibility; citing institutional cores shows available infrastructure and reduces reviewer concerns about resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets should be realistic and aligned with proposed effort and timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure effort, direct costs, and timelines are justified; reviewers and RSP commonly catch unrealistic budgets or mismatched effort allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and administrative completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Address compliance requirements (human/animal subjects, biosafety, COI) and include all required sections and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill in regulatory approvals or plans, include required documents, and correct any compliance gaps before submission to avoid administrative triage or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission administrative checks
rubrics_metrics.description: RSP looks for common pre-submission problems: budget errors (effort, indirect costs), compliance gaps, subaward complications, format violations, and missing required sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional checklists and RSP review to catch these predictable issues; correct subaward documentation and budget line-items early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement (USDA/AFRI emphasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: For USDA NIFA/AFRI proposals, demonstrate stakeholder/producer engagement, extension partnerships, and practical application of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how stakeholders were involved in project design, plans for extension/translation, and multi-state collaborations when relevant; show tangible pathways to on-the-ground impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-disciplinary teams and collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble teams that bring appropriate disciplinary breadth and demonstrate collaborative capacity (multi-state or multi-institutional when useful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document complementary expertise, collaboration management, and, for USDA/large programs, evidence of multi-state or cross-institutional partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts (NSF alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address NSF's two review axes: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts; align Broader Impacts with Wisconsin Idea where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe educational, outreach, or societal benefits clearly; leverage UW extension/engagement programs to strengthen Broader Impacts statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension, education, and outreach components
rubrics_metrics.description: Include education and extension activities appropriate to the funder and the project's aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For land-grant and USDA proposals, show concrete plans for extension, training, K–12 or community engagement, and measurable outreach outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward and collaboration management
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify subaward scopes, budgets, and administrative arrangements to avoid complications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate subaward timing and documentation needs; resolve budget and compliance issues with subrecipients before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and adherence to mechanism-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow funder- and mechanism-specific formatting rules to the letter (page limits, font, sections required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format violations are a common cause of administrative problems; consult mechanism RFAs and institutional templates to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing for non-specialist reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Write so that reviewers outside the immediate subfield can understand significance, approach, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon, provide clear rationale and context, and quickly communicate the problem and solution so reviewers can grasp value in short reading time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate feasibility and include contingencies or alternative approaches if primary strategies fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential pitfalls and alternative plans for each aim to reassure reviewers the project can produce interpretable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: UW academic voice and public service orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect the Wisconsin Idea and land‑grant ethos: public service, community engagement, and practical/translational impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame broader impacts and outreach in terms of state/university service and real-world application; show how research benefits constituents beyond academia.
